# Judith Chapter 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_016_page_001.jpg

---

## THE SONG OF JUDITH

*[Judith's voice — before all Israel]*

**1**
Beat the timbrels for my God!
Ring out the cymbals for my Lord!
Lift a new song to him —
    exalt his name, call out his name!

**2**
For the LORD is the God who shatters wars.
He has pitched his tent in the middle of his people.
He is the one who rescued me
    from the hands of those hunting me down.

**3**
Assur marched down from the mountains of the north
    with ten thousands of his army;
Their mass of soldiers choked every wadi dry,
    their horsemen blanketed the hills.

**4**
He swore he would torch my land,
    cut my young men down with the sword,
hurl my children against the ground,
    hand my little ones over to plunder,
    tear my young women away as his spoil.

**5**
The Lord Almighty put an end to them —
    by the hand of a woman.

**6**
Their champion did not fall to young warriors.
No sons of Titans brought him down.
No towering giants closed in on him.

Judith daughter of Merari brought him down —
    with the beauty of her face.

**7**
She stripped off the widow's mourning
    to lift up the crushed ones of Israel.
She anointed her face with the finest myrrh,

**8**
bound her hair into a tiara,
    dressed herself in linen —
    and walked in to deceive him.

**9**
One look at her sandal
    and his eye was enslaved.
Her beauty seized his soul.
Then the sword found his neck.

**10**
The Persians shuddered at what she dared.
The Medes were left speechless by her audacity.

**11**
Then my lowly ones raised their voices,
    my weak ones shouted —
and the enemy was seized with terror,
    they screamed, they ran.

**12**
Girls' sons pierced them through —
    outcasts' children wounded them —
they fell dead before the face of the LORD my God.

**13**
I will sing a new song to my God.

O Lord — you are great, you are glorious.
You are wondrous in your strength.
Nothing can overcome you.

**14**
Let all your creation serve you.
You spoke — and it came into being.
You breathed out — and it took form.
No one stands against your voice.

**15**
Mountains will shake from their roots.
Waters with them.
Rocks will run like wax before your face.

But to those who fear you —
    you will always show mercy.

**16**
A sweet-smelling offering — it's a small thing to you.
The fat of whole burnt sacrifices — nothing, compared to you.
But the one who fears you?
    That person will be great forever.

**17**
Woe to the nations that raise themselves against my people.
The Lord Almighty will deal with them — on the day of judgment.
He will send fire into their flesh,
    and worms —
and they will cry out in pain
    without end.

---

**18** When they came to Jerusalem, they worshiped God. After the people had purified themselves, they offered burnt offerings, freewill offerings, and their gifts.

**19** And Judith dedicated everything — all the possessions of Holofernes that the people had given her. And the canopy she had taken from his bedchamber she gave to God as a consecrated thing.

**20** For three months the people kept festival before the sanctuary in Jerusalem. Judith stayed with them through all of it.

**21** When it was over, every man returned to his own land. Judith went back to Bethulia and lived on her own estate. For all the rest of her life, she was celebrated throughout Israel.

**22** Many men wanted her. But no man ever knew her — not from the day her husband Manasseh died and was gathered to his people until the end of her own life.

**23** Her fame kept growing. She grew old in her husband's house. She reached one hundred and five years. She gave her servant her freedom. And she died — in Bethulia, the city she had saved — and they buried her in the cave of her husband Manasseh.

**24** The house of Israel mourned her for seven days. Before she died, she gave away everything she owned to those closest to her husband Manasseh, and to those closest to her own family.

**25** And no one ever again spread terror among the sons of Israel —
    not in the days of Judith,
    and not for a long time after she was gone.

---
*PNEUMA notes: The song in vv. 1-17 deliberately echoes both Miriam's song (Exodus 15) and Deborah's song (Judges 5). The timbrels and cymbals of v. 1 echo Miriam (Exodus 15:20). The celebration of a woman warrior echoes Deborah and Jael (Judges 5:24-27). The "new song" formula (vv. 1, 13) appears in Psalms 96 and 98. Verse 5 is the theological thesis of the entire book: the Lord Almighty, by the hand of a woman. Verse 25 is the book's final word. It is deliberately spare — a single sentence that functions as an epitaph for Judith and a summary statement about what her life meant. After this, silence. The silence is the monument.*
